chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported to me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Ubaidah al-Hadhdha, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir Muhammad ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, who said:

In the book of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: Three traits - their possessor does not die until he sees their evil consequences: injustice, severing kinship ties, and false oaths. And indeed, the quickest act of obedience to be rewarded is maintaining kinship ties. Indeed, people may be transgressors, but if they maintain family ties, their wealth grows and they become rich. And indeed, false oaths and severing kinship ties leave the villages as wastelands devoid of their inhabitants.
May Allah bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his family, and grant peace with salutations.

key_terms.البغي: Injustice, transgression, or exceeding proper bounds against others
key_terms.اليمين الكاذبة: A false oath, swearing falsely by God
key_terms.صلة الرحم: Maintaining and nurturing kinship ties and family bonds
key_terms.قطيعة الرحم: Severing kinship ties, cutting off family relations
key_terms.وبال: Evil consequences or severe punishment for one's actions

ai.seo_question: What are the three traits whose evil consequences one sees before death according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmits a teaching from the book of Imam Ali (AS) identifying three destructive traits whose consequences manifest in one's lifetime: injustice (al-baghy), severing kinship ties (qati'at al-rahim), and false oaths (al-yamin al-kadhibah). The teaching contrasts this with the reward of maintaining family bonds, noting that even sinful people prosper when they uphold kinship ties, while false oaths and broken ties lead to the ruin of entire communities.
